# A number as a single-base unit is that many of its base: `var zero
# time.duration = 0`. C holds such a unit as a double and had no rule for the
# conversion ("converting int to duration"). FuzzPipeline found it, from
# testdata/unit_duration_name.sngl.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import time "sngl:time"

var zero time.duration = 0
var some time.duration = 5s

component panel ui.node {
    ui.text #shown(value=zero < some ? "zero" : "set")
}

func testDuration(t test.Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "zero")
    t.assert(zero < some)
}

ui.window {
    panel
}
